paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: God sees every unjust ruler, and He is the Judge of the earth. David opens by asking rulers, "Do you indeed speak justly, O rulers?" (Psalm 58:1), and his answer is no. They plan injustice in their hearts and deal out violence with their hands (Psalm 58:2). Some days it looks like crooked people get away with everything, and this psalm says that is not the end of the story.

Now, this song is rough, and I'll say it once: some of these prayers are heavy. David doesn't hide his anger. He takes it straight to God and asks Him to deal with the wicked (Psalm 58:6). I think that's the lesson for you, baker. When you see unfairness, don't swallow it and don't take matters into your own hands. Bring it to the One who actually sees it all.

Then the song ends with hope. The righteous rejoice, and people say, "There is surely a reward for the righteous! There is surely a God who judges the earth!" (Psalm 58:11). So keep doing right even when nobody notices, because your faithfulness is not wasted. And if you're ever worn out waiting for justice, you can pray like David did and trust God to judge rightly.
